title: proSA: Adjustable MIETHKE Shunt Systems — Your Simple Choice for Precise Patient Care
condition_or_topic: Hydrocephalus treatment with the adjustable proSA gravitational shunt valve and prevention of shunt-related overdrainage
clinical_background: Active people spend about 2/3 of the day upright, and patients with hydrocephalus shunts consequently often face a risk of overdrainage. Gravitational valve technology is presented as a way to avoid the symptoms and long-term complications caused by overdrainage. The proSA permits adjustment to accommodate changes such as growth or increased peritoneal pressure.

main_findings.description: An analysis cited as reference [10] reported that gravitational shunt systems minimised the risk of overdrainage in adults treated for chronic hydrocephalus.
main_findings.context: This is a finding attributed to the cited study, not a result from an original study in this document.

main_findings.description: A report cited as reference [11] stated that adding a gravitational unit to an existing or newly implanted shunt can reduce the occurrence or severity of overdrainage syndrome in children with hydrocephalus and shunts.
main_findings.context: This is a finding attributed to the cited report, not a result from an original study in this document.

interpretation: The brochure presents proSA as an adjustable gravitational valve intended to address overdrainage in patients with hydrocephalus. Its opening pressure changes with body position and can be adjusted during treatment to account for changes in patient characteristics.
comparison_with_prior_evidence: A cited analysis of adult chronic hydrocephalus reports that gravitational shunt systems minimize overdrainage risk. Another cited report states that adding a gravitational unit to a shunt can reduce the occurrence or severity of overdrainage syndrome in children with hydrocephalus. The brochure cites previous work on proGAV, GAV and paediGAV as support for gravitational technology in pediatric and adult hydrocephalus.
clinical_implications: In the supine position, proSA has an opening pressure of 0 cmH2O, so the differential pressure unit determines the opening pressure of the complete shunt system. In the upright position, the pressure settings of the gravitational and differential pressure units are added.
The proSA setting can be adapted over the course of treatment to account for factors such as Body Mass Index, adiposity, pregnancy and pediatric growth.
The brochure states that the “Active Lock” mechanism protects against unintended changes caused by external magnetic fields and that the valve is MR-conditional up to 3 Tesla.
practice_implications: The brochure recommends implanting proSA together with a differential pressure unit.
It recommends a lower opening-pressure setting for patients who are less mobile.

Its initial valve-adjustment guide lists < 5 years: 20 cmH2O; 5-60 years: 25 cmH2O; and > 60 years: 20 cmH2O. These values are not binding, and another setting may be preferable according to the individual patient and anamnesis.

The brochure describes checking the current setting with the verification instrument and confirming an adjustment with the same instrument; it states that adjustment and verification do not require X-ray exposure.
future_directions: Aesculap and Miethke state that they intend to continue investing in research and development, gathering further insights and pursuing solutions for unresolved hydrocephalus-treatment needs.

main_conclusion: The brochure presents proSA as a position-dependent, adjustable gravitational valve intended to expand options for managing hydrocephalus and overdrainage. It recommends implanting proSA with a differential pressure unit and adapting its setting to individual patient characteristics.
narrative_summary:
This manufacturer brochure describes proSA configurations and their use in hydrocephalus care; it does not report a new clinical investigation or original patient outcomes. It frames shunt overdrainage as a concern when patients are upright and cites published work supporting gravitational shunts, including a cited analysis in adults and a cited report on adding a gravitational unit for children with overdrainage syndrome. Those findings are attributed to the cited work, not to a study conducted in this brochure.

The proSA gravitational unit is adjustable from 0 to 40 cmH2O. When a patient is supine, its opening pressure is 0 cmH2O, so the differential pressure unit defines the shunt system’s opening pressure. Upright, the system’s opening pressure equals the settings of both units added together. The brochure recommends combining proSA with a differential pressure unit and setting a lower opening pressure for less mobile patients. Its nonbinding initial-setting table gives 20 cmH2O for patients < 5 years, 25 cmH2O for those 5-60 years and 20 cmH2O for those > 60 years; individual history and characteristics may warrant different settings. It describes adjustment during treatment to account for factors including growth, adiposity and pregnancy. The brochure also states that “Active Lock” protects against unintended magnetic adjustment and that the valve is MR-conditional up to 3 Tesla. Adjustment and verification instruments are presented as allowing settings to be checked without X-ray exposure.

document_sections.heading: Enhanced Patient Care
document_sections.content: Active people spend about 2/3 of each day walking, standing or sitting upright; consequently, people with hydrocephalus who have a shunt may be at risk of overdrainage. proSA builds on gravitational valve technology and permits adjustment to accommodate changes such as growth or increased peritoneal pressure. The document states that gravitational technology introduced ways to avoid symptoms and long-term complications of overdrainage. An analysis cited as [10] concluded that gravitational shunts minimise overdrainage risk in adults with chronic hydrocephalus. Cited publications [1,2,3,4,5] are presented as support for the use of proGAV, GAV and paediGAV in pediatric and adult hydrocephalus. Like proGAV, proSA has an “Active Lock” intended to prevent unintended changes from external magnetic fields; it is described as MR-conditional up to 3 Tesla under ASTM standards [6,7,8,9]. Its adjustment and verification instruments permit settings to be changed and checked without exposing the patient to X-ray [1,9].

document_sections.heading: Enhanced Treatment Options
document_sections.content: The document presents proSA as offering treatment options beyond those of conventional adjustable shunts. Its pressure setting range is 0 to 40 cmH2O, and it can be paired with any differential pressure valve. The set pressure changes its contribution automatically with body position. A titanium housing is described as maintaining function despite external or subcutaneous pressure. A cited report [11] states that adding a gravitational unit to an existing or newly implanted shunt can reduce the occurrence or severity of overdrainage syndrome in children with hydrocephalus. The document distinguishes an adjustable gravitational unit from an optional differential pressure unit.

document_sections.heading: Our Recommendation
document_sections.content: A table gives initial valve adjustments by patient age. The document recommends implanting proSA together with a differential pressure unit. It advises a lower opening-pressure setting for patients with less mobility. The gravitational unit can be readjusted during treatment to account for characteristics such as Body Mass Index, adiposity, pregnancy and pediatric growth. The age-based settings are nonbinding guide values; a patient's characteristics and history may favour another setting.

document_sections.heading: The Function – Supine Function
document_sections.content: proSA is an adjustable gravitational valve whose opening pressure responds to body position. When the patient is supine, its opening pressure is 0 cmH2O, so the differential pressure unit alone determines the shunt's opening pressure. The depicted proSA pressure does not include the differential pressure unit's contribution, which must be added to obtain the opening pressure of the complete shunt.

document_sections.heading: The Function – Upright Function
document_sections.content: In an upright position, both units contribute to the shunt's opening pressure: the overall value is the differential pressure level plus the level selected on the gravitational unit.

document_sections.heading: Localization
document_sections.content: The proSA valve is found by palpation.

document_sections.heading: Verification
document_sections.content: The verification instrument is positioned over the valve as directed in its instructions for use. Pressing its trigger displays the current opening-pressure setting.

document_sections.heading: Adjustment
document_sections.content: The required opening pressure is selected on the adjustment instrument, which is then placed over the valve according to its instructions for use. Gentle pressure on the trigger releases the “Active-Lock” mechanical coupling so the intended setting can be applied. The verification instrument can then confirm the adjustment.

document_sections.heading: proSA®
document_sections.content: proSA is available as an adjustable gravitational unit alone or combined with a differential pressure unit. Its adjustment range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. The listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. The product drawings label an 18 mm gravitational unit, a 14.7 mm differential pressure unit and dimensions of 4.5 mm and 2.8 mm for the illustrated configurations. A product table lists article numbers and the available nonadjustable differential pressure units.

document_sections.heading: proSA® with distal catheter
document_sections.content: This configuration has an integrated distal catheter and is offered with an adjustable gravitational unit alone or together with a differential pressure unit. The gravitational setting range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. Listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm, gravitational unit 18 mm, differential pressure unit 14.7 mm and distal catheter 1200 mm. The drawings also mark dimensions of 4.5 mm and 2.8 mm. A table identifies the article numbers and nonadjustable differential pressure options.

document_sections.heading: proSA® SHUNT SYSTEM with SPRUNG RESERVOIR
document_sections.content: This system combines an adjustable gravitational unit with an integrated distal catheter and a SPRUNG reservoir. Its gravitational range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. The drawing identifies a 20 mm SPRUNG reservoir, a 14.7 mm differential pressure unit, an 18 mm gravitational unit, distal catheter lengths of 600 mm and 1200 mm, and a 180 mm ventricular catheter with an introducing stylet. The listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. According to the document, the flushing reservoir permits a check of ventricular catheter patency and provides distal-only drainage. A table presents article numbers and nonadjustable differential pressure options.

document_sections.heading: proSA® SHUNT SYSTEM with CONTROL RESERVOIR
document_sections.content: This system contains an adjustable gravitational unit, an integrated distal catheter and a Control Reservoir. The gravitational adjustment range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. Its diagram labels a 20 mm Control Reservoir, an 18 mm gravitational unit, a 14.7 mm differential pressure unit, distal catheter lengths of 900 mm and 600 mm, a 180 mm ventricular catheter with introducing stylet, and a deflector marked 9.5 mm and 16 mm. Listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. The reservoir allows ventricular catheter patency to be checked and is described as ensuring drainage only in the distal direction. A table gives article numbers and nonadjustable differential pressure options.

document_sections.heading: proSA® SHUNT SYSTEM with FLUSHING RESERVOIR for pediatric application
document_sections.content: This pediatric configuration has an adjustable gravitational unit, an integrated distal catheter and a pediatric flushing reservoir; combination with a differential pressure unit is optional. The gravitational setting range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. A ventricular catheter is supplied with an introducing stylet and pediatric deflector. The drawing labels a 14 mm flushing reservoir, a 14.7 mm differential pressure unit, an 18 mm gravitational unit, distal catheter lengths of 600 mm and 1200 mm, a deflector marked 6 mm and 10 mm, and a 180 mm ventricular catheter. Listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. A table sets out article numbers and nonadjustable differential pressure options.

document_sections.heading: proSA® SHUNT SYSTEM with BURRHOLE RESERVOIR for pediatric application
document_sections.content: This pediatric system includes an adjustable gravitational unit, an integrated distal catheter and a pediatric burrhole reservoir. It can optionally be combined with a differential pressure unit and includes a ventricular catheter with an introducing stylet. The gravitational range is 0 - 40 cmH2O. The drawing specifies a 14 mm burrhole reservoir, a 14.7 mm differential pressure unit, an 18 mm gravitational unit, distal catheter lengths of 600 mm and 1200 mm, and a 180 mm ventricular catheter. Listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm, differential pressure unit do= 2.8 mm, and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. A table provides article numbers and nonadjustable differential pressure options.

document_sections.heading: proSA® with adjustable differential pressure unit proGAV®
document_sections.content: This configuration pairs an adjustable gravitational unit with an adjustable proGAV differential pressure unit. The gravitational valve range is 0 - 40 cmH2O; the differential pressure unit's table gives 0 – 20. The drawing labels both units as 18 mm. Listed dimensions are connector do= 1.9 mm and catheter di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm.

document_sections.heading: proSA® with adjustable differential pressure unit proGAV® and distal catheter
document_sections.content: This configuration combines adjustable gravitational and differential pressure units with an integrated distal catheter. The gravitational valve range is 0 - 40 cmH2O, and the differential pressure tables for the illustrated variants give 0 – 20. The basic configuration shows an 18 mm differential pressure unit, an 18 mm gravitational unit and a 1200 mm distal catheter. Subsequent illustrated variants incorporate pediatric flushing or burrhole reservoirs and, in some configurations, ventricular catheters, introducing stylets and deflectors. Their labels include 14 mm reservoirs, a 250 mm ventricular catheter, an 85 mm ventricular catheter, a 180 mm ventricular catheter, a 200 mm catheter, and deflector dimensions of 6 mm and 10 mm. Two illustrated burrhole configurations are marked for occipital implantation only. The listed connector dimension is do= 1.9 mm, with catheter dimensions di = 1.2 mm and do= 2.5 mm. The tables identify article numbers for the configurations and their adjustable differential pressure ranges.

document_sections.heading: proSA® Instruments
document_sections.content: The proSA adjustment instrument sets the intended opening pressure, while the verification instrument reads the current setting. The Masterdisc calibrates the verification instrument, and the Compass locates proSA. An adjustment disc permits setting the pressure when skin is thicker. The resterilizable Checkmate enables sterile reading and adjustment before implantation. Instrument tables list the corresponding article numbers and an instrument set.

document_sections.heading: proGAV® Instruments
document_sections.content: For proGAV, an adjustment instrument sets the required opening pressure and a verification instrument reads the current setting. The Masterdisc calibrates the verification instrument; the Compass locates the valve. An adjustment disc is intended for use when skin is thicker, and the resterilizable Checkmate supports sterile reading and setting before implantation. Tables list individual instrument article numbers and a set.

document_sections.heading: Our Shunt Systems – Your Choice
document_sections.content: A comparison table lists proSA, proGAV, GAV, paediGAV, SHUNTASSISTANT, DUALSWITCHVALVE and miniNAV. It describes valve or gravitational-unit type and compares indications, patient characteristics, gravitational assistance and 3 Tesla compatibility. proSA is described as an adjustable gravitational unit intended for combination with a differential pressure valve; proGAV as an adjustable differential pressure valve with a gravitational unit; GAV and paediGAV as gravitational valves for adult and pediatric hydrocephalus, respectively; SHUNTASSISTANT as a gravitational unit used with a differential pressure valve; DUALSWITCHVALVE as a gravitational valve system with a larger CSF flow path; and miniNAV as a small differential pressure valve.

document_sections.heading: Alliance for Innovation
document_sections.content: Aesculap and Miethke describe a collaboration begun in 1999 to develop hydrocephalus treatments. They attribute the introduction of a gravitational unit for pediatric patients to this work and state that the unit can prevent cerebrospinal fluid overdrainage.
